scope: Proposition 3.8 (The graph exterior and its two colours) of the manuscript “Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2” (preprints/Strong-diffeomorphic-approximation-in-three-dimensions-for-p-gt-2-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 368 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 824a96588feb42d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose a small ru,D > 0 in every subcell. In input target coordinates remove the full closed blocks Xi and the open cores of the interval prisms over dD +ru,D(D −dD), with their ends attached to the full blocks. The closure My of the remainder is a locally finite PL three-manifold with boundary. The radial projection in each subcell, identity on subedges, defines a continuous map πT : My −→ Γ, where Γ is the subedge graph. Each component of My is a possibly noncompact graph handlebody. In particular every PL embedded compact interior two-sphere bounds a PL ball and H2(My; Z) = 0. (3.12) For intermediate levels there are two standard families of proper walls: AD(t) is the perimeter at common radial label t, times the face-offset interval; Be(s) is the entire inverse of the intermediate subedge point under πT. Walls within one colour are disjoint. Each A is an incompressible annulus and each B is a disk. An incident pair has two boundary intersection points, one on each annular end; a nonincident pair has none. Consequently transverse individually standard walls with this boundary incidence have one spanning intersection arc for each incident pair, and otherwise only circles; every such circle is contractible in both walls.
